assumptions: Both arms work together, so laterality is bilateral.
The upper arms stay roughly perpendicular to the floor, so the elbow is the only primary moving joint.
The hands are closed on the band throughout, so grip and wrist stability are needed.
The body is supported on the bench, so the trunk and legs need no postural stabilization.
The band is anchored low behind the head, so the upper arms must resist being pulled toward the floor. This calls for shoulder position hold.
The movement is classified as open chain because the hands move freely against band resistance, not against a fixed surface.
classification_reasons: Supine band skull crusher is a bilateral elbow extension with the upper arms held roughly vertical, which the vocabulary can represent.

Both frames show the lifter lying on a bench with both hands holding a band anchored at the base of the rack. The elbows go from flexed in frame 1 to extended in frame 2 while the upper arms stay in place.

instructions: Secure a band to the base of a rack or the bench. Lay on the bench so that the band is lined up with your head.
Take hold of the band, raising your elbows so that the upper arm is perpendicular to the floor. With the elbow flexed, the band should be above your head. This will be your starting position.
Extend through the elbow to straighten your arm, keeping your upper arm in place. Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.
